messages:
alex: Quick thought — our runtime and console are inconsistent for routing fallbacks. Clients often get 200 + a small body saying "fallback", but SDKs treat 200 as success and surface no hint. We should expose a stable client-facing signal.
maria: Can you paste a concrete example of what we're returning today?
alex: Sure — current runtime: ```json
{
  \"status\": \"served\",
  \"backend\": \"fallback-gnx\",
  \"note\": \"degraded throughput\"
}
```
Clients see 200 and don't know it's degraded.
jordan: Yea that's confusing. We can't change 200 semantics for successful responses, but we can add a header or a small top-level field for clients to act on.
samir: Header feels right — less breaking. e.g. `x-redwood-client-status: fallback;reason=cap;rate=0.3` — SDKs can parse that and surface to app.
emily: +1 for user-friendly hints too. We should include a short hint string that UI teams can show: `user_hint=\"We're serving a lower-capacity model. Expect slightly altered quality.\"`
maria: Concern: exposing internal codes (backend names) in headers could leak our infra. We should expose generic enums only (fallback, degraded, throttled, quota, internal_error). Keep internal_code in logs only.
jordan: Agreed. Proposal: two things — `x-redwood-client-status` (stable enum) + optional `x-redwood-client-hint` (short human hint). Internal code goes to `x-rw-internal-code` (only for audit logs, not recommended for public docs).
alex: Example header proposal: ```
x-redwood-client-status: degraded; reason=capacity
x-redwood-client-hint: Served from fallback model; reduce concurrency or try dedicated
```
ops-bot: deploy notice — canary runtime v2.3 rolled to 12% of hostpool at 2026-03-18T10:02Z :rocket:
samir: Telemetry question — do we want `client_exposed_status` events so console can show historical % fallback? If so we need schema: event.count, status(enum), tenant_id, sampled boolean.
emily: Yes — console should show rolling 1h/24h percent with sample rate. Also show last runbook link for that status. e.g., `https://console/runbook/fallback_capacity`
maria: UX copy: avoid scary language. Use 'Degraded' over 'Fallback' in user UI. But keep enum as `fallback` for clarity in API. Map in console: `fallback -> Degraded (lower capacity)`.
jordan: We need to update SDKs to surface both header and hint; fallback to console docs for runbook link via telemetry. Also update HTTP contract doc.
alex: Minor API detail — some clients can't read headers (web browsers with fetch CORS). Should we also include a short top-level field `client_status` in the JSON for those cases? It must be non-breaking and optional.
samir: If it's optional and only used when present, ok. But avoid duplicating sensitive internal info. Field example: ```json
{
  \"client_status\": \"fallback\",
  \"client_hint\": \"Serving lower-capacity model; consider retrying later\",
  \"data\": { ... }
}
```
emily: We'll need consistent i18n for `client_hint` if we surface to end-users. For console, english is fine but SDKs should not auto-display it without app owner's choice.
maria: Action items: alex PR for header + optional field in API spec, due EOD Thu. I'll update console badge mapping to show percent and runbook link (maria). jordan to review SDK mapping and CORS considerations. samir to add telemetry event schema and sample rate knob. emily to draft user-facing copy variants (short / expanded).
alex: Cool. One last edge — quota vs throttle. For quota exceed we should still return 429 and standard body. For soft-degrades we keep 200 but add `client_status=degraded`.
jordan: Noted. We'll include mapping in the RFC: 
- 429 -> quota_throttle (exposed via status code)
- 503/5xx -> backend_error (opaque to clients)
- 200 + client_status=degraded -> soft-degrade path

samir: I'll prototype telemetry and add `client_exposed_status` to event schema. Will include `sample_rate` header for high-throughput tenants to control costs.
emily: ok, I'll prep copy for product and support to avoid surprises.
ops-bot: reminder — RFC draft created at https://git.redwood/rfcs/client-status-exposure (alex)
alex: Thanks everyone. We'll iterate in the RFC. If no objections, I'll start the PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
